aula.objetivo: Introduce yourself, ask for someone's name and origin, and use «sein» in the present tense with «du», «ihr» and «Sie».

blocos.titulo: Hallo! Wie heißt du? / Hi! What's your name?
blocos.contexto: Lea and Paul meet in line at a language course.

linhas.ru: — Hallo! Ich heiße Lea. Wie heißt du?
linhas.pt: — Hi! I'm called Lea. What's your name?
linhas.audio: Hallo! Ich heiße Lea. Wie heißt du?

linhas.pt: — Where do you come from, Paul?

linhas.ru: — Ich komme aus Brasilien. Und du?
linhas.pt: — I come from Brazil. And you?
linhas.audio: Ich komme aus Brasilien. Und du?

linhas.pt: — Nice to meet you too, Paul!

blocos.titulo: Word order and the first questions
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: listen to «Ich heiße Lea.» and then «Wie heißt du?». To say your name, the verb is «heißen», which means to be called. STEP 2: in German, the conjugated verb always sits in SECOND position in the sentence. In «Ich heiße Lea», «ich» takes the first position and «heiße» takes the second. STEP 3: in questions with a question word, that word comes first. Examples: «wie», which means how and sounds like «vee» (German «w» sounds like English «v», and «ie» sounds like «ee»), and «woher», which means where from and sounds like «voh-HAIR». The verb stays second: «Wie heißt du?» and «Woher kommst du?». Notice that German has no «do» here: English says «Where do you come from?», but German simply says «Woher kommst du?». STEP 4: in a yes/no question, the verb moves to the front: «Heißt du Lea?». Answer «Ja» or «Nein». STEP 5: the verb ending changes with the person. With «ich», it ends in «e»: «ich heiße», «ich komme». With «du», it ends in «st»: «du kommst». In «heißen», the «ß» already makes the «ss» sound, so you add only the «t»: «du heißt». STEP 6: don't forget the pronoun. English needs «I» (you can't say «Come from Brazil» for «I come from Brazil»), and German is the same: «Ich komme aus Brasilien». STEP 7: a heads-up. In the words «der Name» and «der Vorname», «der» is an article, one of the German words for «the». You learn articles in lesson 3. For now, repeat «der» together with the word.
blocos.comparacao: in English, the verb changes only in the third person («I come», «she comes»). In German it changes for almost every person («ich komme», «du kommst», «sie kommt»), so the ending tells you who is speaking. English also uses «do» in questions («Where do you come from?»), and German does not: the verb simply moves to second position. And «Ich heiße Lea» is literally «I am called Lea», not «my name is Lea».

linhas.pt: What is your name? My name is Anna.
What is your name? (formal) My name is Müller.
Where do you come from? I come from Brazil.
Where do you come from? (formal) I come from Brazil.

erros.motivo: The conjugated verb stays in second position, right after «ich».
In a question with «wie», the verb comes right after the question word.
The pronoun «ich» cannot disappear. In English you also say «I», never just «Am Anna».

itens.explicacao: You hear «vee hyst doo»: asking for a name uses the verb «heißen». «Woher kommst du?» asks where someone is from, and «Wie geht’s?» asks how the person is.
The sentence has the verb «komme» and ends with «Brasilien». «Ich heiße Paul» gives a name, and «Hamburg» is a different place.
Write «heiße» with «ß», which sounds like «ss». The verb comes right after «ich», in second position.
Reviewing lesson 1: «Guten Morgen» is the morning greeting, and the person's name follows, separated by a comma.
With «ich», the verb ends in «e»: «ich heiße». The form «heißt» belongs to «du», «er» or «ihr».
With «du», the verb ends in «st»: «du kommst». The ending «e» belongs to «ich», and the ending «t» to «er».
The conjugated verb stays in second position, right after «ich». The order «Heiße ich Paul?» would be a yes/no question.

itens.enunciado: Put in order: «Where do you come from?»
itens.explicacao: The question word «Woher» comes first, the verb «kommst» stays second and «du» follows.

itens.enunciado: Put in order: «Are you called Lea?»
itens.explicacao: In a yes/no question, the verb opens the sentence: «Heißt», then «du», then the name.

blocos.enunciado: Say out loud: «Hallo! Ich heiße … Ich komme aus Brasilien. Freut mich!». Then ask both questions to a real or imaginary person: «Wie heißt du? Woher kommst du?». If you can, record yourself for 20 seconds and listen back.
Listen again to the greetings from the previous lesson and repeat: «Hallo», «Guten Morgen», «Guten Tag», «Guten Abend», «Wie geht’s?» and «Tschüs». Then read «ich», «Schule» and «Buch» out loud.
